textbook: Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a SINGLE human oocyte (egg cell), a large round human germ cell, centered in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with lots of negative space around structures for later labels. Fill the whole square edge-to-edge on a neutral dark charcoal background with NO border, frame, vignette or letterbox. Match the exact house look of a refined educational plate: a MUTED, slightly desaturated palette (soft dusty tints, never bright primary or cartoon colours), THIN clean outlines (not heavy black strokes), gentle soft shading, each structure its own distinct soft colour fill. The oocyte is a large sphere. Around it, a thick pale translucent lavender-white shell (the zona pellucida) surrounds the cell, with a thin fluid gap (perivitelline space) between the shell and the cell membrane. Outside the shell, a ring of small rounded soft-pink follicle cells sits directly against it (corona radiata), with a looser cluster of similar small pink cells further out (cumulus oophorus), both clearly attached, not floating separately. A neat quarter cut-away of the oocyte itself reveals the interior: warm cream-beige granular cytoplasm (ooplasm) filling most of the cell, a soft blue-violet barrel-shaped meiotic spindle positioned off-centre near the cortex with a single tiny pale sphere (the first polar body) beside it in the perivitelline space, a thin band of small golden-orange dots just under the cell membrane (cortical granules), many small teal-green oval mitochondria dispersed through the cytoplasm, scattered pale-yellow lipid droplets and nutrient granules, and a modest cluster of soft lavender-grey Golgi/ER ribbons near the spindle. Anatomically faithful human egg cell. Do NOT draw a cell wall, chloroplasts, a central vacuole, nucleoid, plasmids, or any flagellum/cilia on the oocyte itself; this is NOT a plant cell, NOT a bacterium, and the oocyte does not swim. Show only ONE nucleus/spindle and ONE first polar body, no second polar body. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows, or watermarks in the image.
